groups.title: Orchestrator
groups.intro: Start here if you have been handed a task and do not know which skill does it. This one routes.

skills.name: medical-affairs-orchestrator
skills.summary: Route any Medical Affairs request to the right workflow and run it end to end.
skills.produces: A routed, executed Medical Affairs workflow

skills.name: workshop-launcher
skills.summary: Start a Medical Affairs workshop from a repository link or a simple request.
skills.produces: A prepared and executed synthetic workshop mission

groups.title: Foundation — the core
groups.intro: medical-affairs-foundations loads on every Medical Affairs task, without exception: it carries the compliance boundary and the adverse-event escalation rule. The others load when the task reaches them — evidence appraisal when interpreting study data, citation integrity when the deliverable will carry references, quality review at stage 4, capability detection when producing a file.

skills.name: capability-detection
skills.summary: Work out what this runtime can actually do before promising a deliverable, and degrade visibly rather than failing.
skills.produces: Capability report and a resolved output strategy

skills.name: citation-integrity
skills.summary: Check that every factual claim traces to a real, retrievable source that actually says what it is cited for.
skills.produces: Verified reference list with evidence tiers

skills.name: deliverable-quality-review
skills.summary: Red-team your own Medical Affairs deliverable before anyone else sees it.
skills.produces: Review findings with severity, and a revised deliverable

skills.name: evidence-appraisal
skills.summary: Critically appraise clinical evidence the way an experienced Medical Affairs scientist does — before summarising, citing or building strategy on it.
skills.produces: Appraised evidence with stated certainty and limitations

skills.name: medical-affairs-foundations
skills.summary: The operating principles, compliance boundaries and safety obligations that govern all Medical Affairs work.
skills.produces: Compliance and safety frame applied to every other skill

groups.title: Reasoning primitives — composed by the workflows
groups.intro: Usually reached as a dependency rather than chosen: the workflow skills call these to do the actual thinking. strategic-analysis is the exception and is routable directly, for a request that is purely "so what should we do about it" with no workflow behind it.

skills.name: evidence-synthesis
skills.summary: Turn a body of clinical evidence into a defensible narrative that states what the totality supports, what it does not, and where it disagrees with itself.
skills.produces: Evidence narrative with stated certainty and open questions

skills.name: insight-generation
skills.summary: Turn raw observations into insights that change a decision.
skills.produces: Insight set with implications and actions

skills.name: strategic-analysis
skills.summary: Reason about Medical Affairs strategy rather than generating activity lists.
skills.produces: Prioritised strategic choices with stated assumptions and trade-offs

groups.title: Data and search — live external evidence
groups.intro: These retrieve or prepare public, supplied and local evidence. Public literature, trial registry, and label/safety databases need network access; local data and supplied transcripts do not. See docs/api-setup.md.

skills.name: clinical-trials-search
skills.summary: Search ClinicalTrials.gov via the v2 API to map the trial landscape — what is running, by whom, in which populations, with what endpoints, and what is about to read out.
skills.produces: Trial landscape with sponsors, phases, endpoints and timelines

skills.name: data-connection
skills.summary: Connect Medical Affairs work to available data using authorized connectors, exported files or read-only database queries.
skills.produces: Connection assessment, field mapping and sourced data extract

skills.name: medical-terminology-mapping
skills.summary: Resolve free-text clinical language to controlled vocabulary so insights, adverse events, conditions and interventions can be counted and compared consistently.
skills.produces: Concept-to-code mappings with confidence and unresolved list

skills.name: meeting-transcription
skills.summary: Turn an audio recording or supplied transcript into reviewable Medical Affairs meeting material.
skills.produces: Transcript with provenance, correction queue and downstream handoff

skills.name: public-evidence-search
skills.summary: Search free public scientific sources through the bundled gateway when a task needs literature, trial records, labels, adverse-event reports or citation metadata.
skills.produces: Retrieved public evidence with query and access status

skills.name: pubmed-search
skills.summary: Search PubMed properly and retrieve real, verifiable literature via the NCBI E-utilities API.
skills.produces: Verified literature result set with search strategy recorded

skills.name: regulatory-label-intelligence
skills.summary: Retrieve approved US label content and post-marketing safety data via openFDA, and interpret both correctly.
skills.produces: Label-grounded product facts and correctly-caveated safety context

skills.name: systematic-literature-review
skills.summary: Run a reproducible, PRISMA-aligned systematic literature review — protocol first, documented search strategy, screening funnel with recorded exclusion reasons, structured extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment.
skills.produces: PRISMA-aligned systematic review with flow diagram and evidence tables

groups.title: Workflows — the core tasks
groups.intro: One per recurring Medical Affairs workflow. Each produces a named deliverable and runs the six-stage execution contract in AGENTS.md.

skills.name: advisory-board-design
skills.summary: Design and run an advisory board that produces advice rather than agreement — charter, questions, advisor selection, fair market value, discussion design, and output that changes a decision.
skills.produces: Advisory board charter, questions and materials

skills.name: competitive-intelligence
skills.summary: Track and interpret competitor scientific activity continuously — pipeline movement, publication patterns, evidence strategy, regulatory milestones and positioning shifts, and what they signal.
skills.produces: Competitive intelligence assessment

skills.name: congress-intelligence
skills.summary: Analyse what changed at a medical congress and what the organisation should do about it — not summarise what was presented.
skills.produces: Congress intelligence readout

skills.name: evidence-gap-analysis
skills.summary: Identify what we still do not know, decide which gaps are worth closing, and propose how.
skills.produces: Prioritised evidence gap analysis with research proposals

skills.name: executive-briefing
skills.summary: Distil any body of Medical Affairs work into the two-page brief or ten-slide read a leadership team actually absorbs — situation, what changed, what it means, what to decide, by when.
skills.produces: Executive briefing (two-page memo or short deck)

skills.name: field-insight-synthesis
skills.summary: Turn a body of field medical observations into insights leadership can act on.
skills.produces: Field insight report with ranked insights and actions

skills.name: field-medical-planning
skills.summary: Plan the field medical function over a cycle — territory and account prioritisation, MSL objectives, engagement planning across a stakeholder map, capacity modelling, and the metrics that describe scientific impact rather than activity volume.
skills.produces: Field medical plan with prioritised accounts, objectives and capacity

skills.name: guideline-engagement
skills.summary: Understand and engage with clinical practice guideline development — committee cycles, what evidence a guideline body will accept, whether current evidence could support inclusion, and planning against timelines far longer than a medical plan.
skills.produces: Guideline landscape assessment and evidence readiness plan

skills.name: hcp-discovery-and-access
skills.summary: Identify relevant HCPs and ethical institutional access routes for scientific engagement.
skills.produces: Verified candidate register and institution-aware scientific access plan

skills.name: integrated-evidence-plan
skills.summary: Build the cross-functional evidence plan for an asset — every study, analysis and publication across clinical development, Medical Affairs, HEOR and market access, sequenced against the decisions and milestones each has to serve.
skills.produces: Integrated evidence plan with sequencing, owners and decision links

skills.name: investigator-initiated-study-review
skills.summary: Evaluate and govern investigator-initiated study proposals — IIS, ISR, IIT, investigator-sponsored research.
skills.produces: IIS proposal assessment and recommendation

skills.name: kol-engagement-brief
skills.summary: Prepare an MSL or medical lead for a specific scientific exchange with a named external expert.
skills.produces: KOL engagement brief

skills.name: launch-field-training
skills.summary: Design the training and certification that make field medical teams able to handle launch conversations — the data, its limitations, the questions nobody can answer yet, unsolicited off-label requests and adverse event escalation — tested by scenario rather than recall.
skills.produces: Field launch curriculum, scenario bank and certification plan

skills.name: launch-medical-readiness
skills.summary: Assess whether Medical Affairs is actually ready for a launch, label expansion or major data readout — and say plainly where it is not.
skills.produces: Launch readiness assessment with a verdict

skills.name: launch-timeline-and-governance
skills.summary: Build the Medical Affairs launch critical path and the governance that runs it — workback from the decision date, dependencies on label wording and publication, gate criteria written before the gate, named owners, and what moves when the date moves.
skills.produces: Launch critical path, gate criteria and governance plan with named owners

skills.name: literature-surveillance
skills.summary: Run ongoing literature and evidence surveillance — a repeatable watch on a topic, product, class or competitor that reports what is NEW since the last cycle and what it changes, rather than a one-off search.
skills.produces: Surveillance cycle report with delta, appraisal and implications

skills.name: medical-affairs-metrics
skills.summary: Measure whether Medical Affairs work changed anything, rather than counting how much of it happened.
skills.produces: Metric set with definitions, sources and interpretation limits

skills.name: medical-content-operations
skills.summary: Plan and maintain non-promotional Medical Affairs content across channels using audience needs, evidence, content inventories and engagement measures.
skills.produces: Audience-channel plan, content register and evidence-change impact list

skills.name: medical-education-program
skills.summary: Design independent medical education and company-organised scientific education — IME grant strategy, curricula, needs assessments, speaker programmes and their governance, symposia and preceptorships.
skills.produces: Education programme design, needs assessment and governance plan

skills.name: medical-information-response
skills.summary: Draft responses to unsolicited medical enquiries from healthcare professionals, patients and payers, and build the standard response documents and FAQ library behind them.
skills.produces: Standard response document or scientific response letter

skills.name: medical-launch-plan
skills.summary: Build the entire Medical Affairs launch plan for an upcoming asset, new indication or label expansion by running a coordinated team of digital workers — one per launch workstream, each given its own context — under a Launch Lead, with humans deciding at every gate.
skills.produces: Integrated medical launch plan with workstream plans, critical path, owners and human decision gates

skills.name: medical-strategy-plan
skills.summary: Build or challenge a medical plan — the scientific priorities, the choices behind them, and the activities that trace to them.
skills.produces: Medical plan with prioritised scientific objectives

skills.name: msl-administrative-operations
skills.summary: Reduce repetitive MSL administration by assembling source-backed meeting packs, open-task queues, draft CRM imports, weekly summaries and coverage reports.
skills.produces: Prioritized administrative queue, draft record packet and weekly status brief

skills.name: msl-post-call-follow-up
skills.summary: Convert actual MSL engagement notes or a transcript into factual CRM-ready drafts, scientific follow-up tasks and evidence-gap records.
skills.produces: Draft CRM note, follow-up task list and scientific-question register

skills.name: msl-pre-call-planning
skills.summary: Prepare an MSL for an upcoming scientific HCP engagement using verified professional context, prior interactions, unresolved enquiries, current evidence and permitted materials.
skills.produces: One-page pre-call brief, evidence pack and unresolved-question list

skills.name: patient-engagement-planning
skills.summary: Design Medical Affairs partnerships and co-creation with patients, caregivers and patient organizations around scientific needs.
skills.produces: Patient engagement plan with accessibility, feedback and evidence priorities

skills.name: payer-value-dossier
skills.summary: Build evidence for payers and health technology assessment bodies — AMCP format dossiers, NICE, G-BA and HAS submissions, value propositions, budget impact narratives, and responses to HTA critique.
skills.produces: Payer value dossier or HTA evidence submission

skills.name: promotional-material-medical-review
skills.summary: Support a qualified medical signatory reviewing commercial promotional material by assessing that every claim is scientifically accurate, substantiated by the referenced data, and fairly balanced.
skills.produces: Draft medical review findings and recommendation for the signatory

skills.name: real-world-evidence-design
skills.summary: Design a real-world evidence study that will survive scrutiny — target trial emulation, data source selection, the estimand, confounding control, and a protocol written and registered before the data are touched.
skills.produces: RWE study concept or protocol with the estimand and design stated

skills.name: safety-communication
skills.summary: Communicate safety information to healthcare professionals and internal audiences — new safety findings, label safety changes, emerging signals, responses to safety questions, and the decision about whether and how to communicate at all.
skills.produces: Safety communication plan and content

skills.name: scientific-communication-strategy
skills.summary: Decide what the publication and scientific communication strategy should be — which questions to answer, for which audiences, in what sequence — rather than listing papers by data availability.
skills.produces: Scientific communication strategy and prioritised publication plan

skills.name: scientific-platform
skills.summary: Build or challenge the scientific platform — the core evidence-based narrative, the scientific statements it supports, the lexicon, and the communication objectives everything else derives from.
skills.produces: Scientific platform with substantiated statements

groups.title: Content generation — the deliverables
groups.intro: Turn analysis into the artefact somebody actually receives: a deck, a manuscript, an abstract, a poster, a lay summary, a review pack.

skills.name: congress-abstract-and-poster
skills.summary: Write congress abstracts that fit the submission rules and build the posters that follow them.
skills.produces: Congress abstract and poster (.pptx)

skills.name: consulting-grade-design
skills.summary: The shared visual language every generated deliverable follows — palette, typography, chart furniture, layout and image use — so a deck, PDF, HTML report or figure leaves looking like it came from a top-tier advisory firm.
skills.produces: Design system applied across every generated deliverable

skills.name: data-visualization-for-medical
skills.summary: Produce clinical trial figures that are honest and interpretable — Kaplan- Meier curves with numbers at risk, forest plots, waterfall and spider plots, adverse event figures, PRISMA flow diagrams.
skills.produces: Publication-quality clinical figures

skills.name: diagram-and-schema
skills.summary: Draw the diagrams Medical Affairs actually needs — treatment pathways, study schemas, PRISMA flow diagrams, patient journeys, evidence maps, decision trees, mechanism-of-action schematics, and governance flows.
skills.produces: Diagram (Mermaid, SVG or ASCII)

skills.name: document-ingestion
skills.summary: Read documents someone has given you — PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV.
skills.produces: Extracted document text, tables and structure

skills.name: interactive-html-report
skills.summary: Build a self-contained HTML report that opens in any browser with no dependencies — evidence dashboards, insight reports with filterable tables, congress readouts, competitive landscapes, evidence gap trackers.
skills.produces: Self-contained interactive HTML report

skills.name: library-menu
skills.summary: Explain what this entire library can do and render the visual menu card that shows it — every skill grouped by the workflow it serves, as prose, a table or an SVG/PNG infographic for a README, a slide or a stakeholder walkthrough.
skills.produces: Library capability overview and menu-card infographic (SVG/PNG)

skills.name: medical-correspondence
skills.summary: Write the formal correspondence Medical Affairs sends — Dear Healthcare Professional letters, responses to investigators and institutions, agency and vendor briefs, advisory board invitations, author correspondence, and letters accompanying scientific responses.
skills.produces: Formal medical correspondence

skills.name: medical-slide-deck
skills.summary: Build non-promotional medical slide decks — advisory board decks, MSL scientific presentations, congress readouts, medical-to-medical (M2M) presentations, internal data reviews and training material.
skills.produces: Non-promotional medical slide deck (.pptx)

skills.name: mlr-review-readiness
skills.summary: Prepare Medical Affairs content for Medical/Legal/Regulatory review and pre-check it against what reviewers actually reject.
skills.produces: Claim-evidence matrix and MLR submission pack

skills.name: pdf-generation
skills.summary: Produce PDF deliverables — briefs, reports, standard response documents, one-pagers, evidence summaries, anything that must look the same for every reader and print predictably.
skills.produces: PDF deliverable (or print-ready HTML)

skills.name: plain-language-summary
skills.summary: Write plain language summaries of clinical research for patients and the public — trial results lay summaries, plain language summaries of publications, and patient-facing scientific material.
skills.produces: Plain language summary

skills.name: scientific-manuscript
skills.summary: Draft, structure and prepare a scientific manuscript for journal submission — primary trial reports, secondary analyses, real-world evidence papers, reviews and case reports.
skills.produces: Manuscript draft (.docx) with reporting-guideline checklist

skills.name: spreadsheet-analysis
skills.summary: Analyse and produce spreadsheets — field insight exports, enquiry logs, publication trackers, evidence tables, budget allocations, congress abstract lists.
skills.produces: Spreadsheet analysis or a generated workbook

skills.name: visual-abstract
skills.summary: Create visual abstracts and infographics that summarise a study or a body of evidence honestly.
skills.produces: Visual abstract or infographic (SVG)
